messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testJira567` is testing the behavior of the method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` when arrays of different but related types are combined. The first call with `Number[]` works fine because `Integer` and `Long` are both subclasses of `Number`. The second call attempts to combine `Integer[]` and `Long[]` which results in an `ArrayStoreException` at runtime.

Inspecting the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method shows that it creates a new array of the component type of `array1` (in the failing case, `Integer.class`), then it copies `array1` and `array2` into the new array using `System.arraycopy`. The new array's type is fixed to the component type of the first array, but the second array's component type may not be compatible for storage in the new array (Long cannot be stored in Integer[]), causing the `ArrayStoreException`.

The current behavior is problematic because the exception is a runtime `ArrayStoreException` and not an `IllegalArgumentException` as the test expects for mismatched array types. The test suggests it would be clearer and safer to detect this incompatibility earlier and throw `IllegalArgumentException` with a clearer message instead of failing with a raw system array copy error.

No information from recent bug reports indicates relevant fixes related to this issue.

Thus, the root cause is the method's assumption that the component type of the first array can hold all elements from both arrays, which is not always true. This leads to a system array store exception. The method lacks proper validation for mixed array types before creating and copying arrays.

This diagnosis fully explains the test failure and matches the issue reported that the current exception is not clear and suggests better type compatibility checks.

Next, I will identify methods likely responsible for fixing this behavior.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
